claims.text: DIA document numbers follow the pattern DIA-08-YYMM-NNN, where 08 ties to the FY2008 program start and YYMM is the production month — e.g. DIA-08-0911-016 (Nov 2009), DIA-08-1003-015 (Mar 2010), DIA-08-1102-007 (Feb 2011 batch). The numbering is sparse in the released set, which indicates the released DIRDs are not the complete numbered series.

claims.text: THE MOST CHECKABLE FINDING THE PROPULSION STRAND PRODUCED, AND IT IS ABOUT THIS SERIES. DIRD DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', cover-dated 30 March 2010 under the 'Acquisition Threat Support' banner, 45 pages as released, attributed on the DIA list of 9 January 2018 to Dr Eric Davis of EarthTech International, DOES NOT MENTION THOMAS TOWNSEND BROWN. Word counts over the whole released PDF, taken 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, Podkletnov 0. 'Brown' occurs three times and every one of them is the surname of a different author in the reference list: L. S. Brown and Maclay, 'Vacuum Stress between Conducting Plates', Physical Review 184 (1969); H. R. Brown as co-editor of 'The Philosophy of Vacuum' (1991); and J. H. Brownell on Casimir photons (2008). Alcubierre occurs once, as reference [43].

claims.text: WHAT THE ZERO-COUNTS ARE AND ARE NOT EVIDENCE FOR, stated so no later session overstates them. THEY ARE EVIDENCE that the United States government's own commissioned survey of antigravity for aerospace applications, written under the same programme this board maps, is a review of gravitomagnetic forces, Forward's dipole generator, Felber's effect, negative energy, dark energy, the cosmological constant and quantum vacuum zero-point fluctuation force, and that it never reaches for the figure the electrogravitics literature treats as its origin. THEY ARE NOT EVIDENCE that DIA considered Brown and rejected him: the document shows no sign of having considered him at all, and an absence is not an adjudication. THEY ARE NOT EVIDENCE that Brown's work was suppressed, hidden or classified; nothing opened supports that and nothing here asserts it.

sources.title: NASA/TM-2004-213082, Marc G. Millis, 'Prospects for Breakthrough Propulsion from Physics', NASA Glenn Research Center, 19 pages

claims.text: Stated inference, and it is about transparency rather than content. Between 1996 and 2002 NASA ran a public, funded, unclassified assessment of exotic propulsion, named the claims it examined, published which of sixteen tasks failed, and closed. Between 2009 and 2011 DIA commissioned thirty-eight reference documents covering overlapping subject matter, released them only under FOIA, and withheld every author under exemption (b)(6). NOTHING OPENED JOINS THE TWO PROGRAMMES TO EACH OTHER and no institutional edge between them is proposed; Marc Millis wrote for both, which is a fact about a person and not a link between the institutions.

desc: Series of ~38 unclassified technical reports produced under AAWSAP by BAASS subcontractors and published by DIA in two series lines: 'Acquisition Threat Support' (FY2009 tranche, published 2009-2010) and 'Defense Futures' (FY2010 tranche, published 2010-2011).

claims.text: The Defense Intelligence Agency released thirty-seven of the thirty-eight AAWSAP Defense Intelligence Reference Documents to The Black Vault on 25 March 2022, completing FOIA case FOIA-0159-2018, which had been filed on 31 January 2018.

The one report not released was the SECRET-classified version of 'State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons'; it was not referenced as withheld in the release documentation, so the administrative appeal was filed on the adequacy of DIA's search rather than on an exemption.

The released series includes 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions' (DIRD 13, 33 pages), 'Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering' (DIRD 15, 17 pages) and 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy' (DIRD 18, 42 pages).

The released series includes 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications' (DIRD 19, 44 pages), 'The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research' (DIRD 14, 16 pages) and 'Negative Mass Propulsion' (DIRD 29, 43 pages).

The released series includes 'Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues' (DIRD 26, 38 pages), a survey of physiological effects on humans from proximity to anomalous fields.
The released series includes 'Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight' (DIRD 28, 57 pages), a human-factors assessment of operating a vehicle with capabilities beyond current aerospace technology.

The released series includes 'Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications' (DIRD 22), 'Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter' (DIRD 02), 'Materials for Advanced Aerospace Platforms' (DIRD 05), 'Metallic Glasses - Status and Prospects for Aerospace Applications' (DIRD 01) and 'Invisibility Cloaking - Theory and Experiments' (DIRD 07).

The subject coverage of the series maps onto the twelve technical areas specified in the AAWSAP Statement of Objectives of 18 July 2008: lift, propulsion, control, power generation, spatial/temporal translation, materials, configuration and structure, signature reduction, human interface, human effects, armament, and peripheral areas.

Eric Davis stated in a Coast to Coast AM interview on 28 January 2018 that while working for Bigelow Aerospace/BAASS he and colleagues created thirty-eight Defense Intelligence Reference Documents under AAWSAP, which is what triggered the FOIA request that eventually produced the release.
A separate FOIA case, FOIA-0033-2019, produced a listing breakdown of the reports in January 2019, a slightly different version of which had already leaked before official release.

AARO characterises the DIRDs as 'exploratory papers addressing the 12 scientific areas tasked in the contract's statement of work' and states that 'These scientific papers were never thoroughly peer reviewed.'

AARO states that the DIRDs represent essentially the whole of what AAWSAP produced, that it 'has yet to uncover any other substantive UAP case work conducted by AAWSAP/AATIP,' and that the remainder of the effort consisted of case reviews, interviews of observers, and work on alleged paranormal activity at the contractor principal's Utah property.

No released DIRD reports the examination of recovered material or describes a recovered craft; the released series consists of literature surveys and theoretical assessments, several of which conclude the routes examined are not presently achievable.
The tasking record showing who inside DIA selected the thirty-eight DIRD topics, and on what basis each was chosen, has not been released.

claims.source: https://www.twz.com/26056/heres-the-list-of-studies-the-militarys-secretive-ufo-program-funded-some-were-junk (Joseph Trevithick, The War Zone, 18 January 2019); original document at https://fas.org/blogs/secrecy/2019/01/aatip-list/ - DEMOTED from Tier 1 (cited to a secondary/encyclopedic source); needs primary replacement
claims.text: DIA compiled the list of all products produced under the AATIP contract at the request of the offices of Senator John McCain and Senator Jack Reed of the Senate Armed Services Committee; the five-page document was obtained by Steven Aftergood of the Federation of American Scientists under FOIA on 16 January 2019.

claims.source: DIA cover letter reproduced and quoted verbatim at https://www.twz.com/26056/heres-the-list-of-studies-the-militarys-secretive-ufo-program-funded-some-were-junk
claims.text: The DIA cover letter states: "Based on interest from your staff regarding the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)'s role in the Advanced Aviation Threat Identification Program (AATIP) please find attached a list of all products produced under the AATIP contract for DIA to publish," and "The purpose of AATIP was to investigate foreign advanced aerospace weapons threats from the present out to the next 40 years."

The program officially began in 2007 as the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) program; between 2008 and 2012 DIA spent approximately $22 million and produced a total of 38 reports.

claims.source: https://www.twz.com/26056/heres-the-list-of-studies-the-militarys-secretive-ufo-program-funded-some-were-junk (Bigelow contract award); contract number and original bid solicitation archived at https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/advanced-aerospace-weapon-systems-applications-program-aawsap-original-bid-solicitation/
claims.text: Bigelow Aerospace won the AATIP contract and managed its research; the contract was performed by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) under DIA contract HHM402-08-C-0072.
The BAASS technical reports were converted into Defense Intelligence Reference Documents by DIA's James T. Lacatski.
DIA placed AATIP under its Defense Warning Office, a unit monitoring threats to U.S. interests in critical regions since its creation in 2002.

Hal Puthoff and Eric Davis of EarthTech International (Austin, Texas) were primary authors on six of the 38 reports between them, and Davis is co-author on a seventh from independent consultant Richard Obousy; because the DIA list records only the primary author, the full EarthTech contribution cannot be determined from the document.

Exactly one of the 38 reports was produced in two versions, one classified Secret with instructions not to release it to foreign nationals — the high energy laser weapon development report from Directed Technologies, Inc. Every other product is labelled 'For Official Use Only.'

Named contributors include Ulf Leonhardt (University of St Andrews, 'Invisibility Cloaking'), Lockheed Martin (three reports, including one on fusion power and one titled 'Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications'), George Hathaway of Hathaway Consulting, Paul Czysz (retired USAF officer and McDonnell Douglas engineer), Marc Millis (former NASA propulsion engineer, Tau Zero Foundation), and Robert Baker (GravWave).

DIA funded a high-frequency gravitational wave report from Robert Baker's GravWave after the JASON advisory group had, in 2008, reviewed Baker's separate HFGW work for ODNI and concluded: 'The proposed applications of the science of HFGW are fundamentally wrong' and 'No foreign threat in HFGW is credible.'
More than half of the 38 studies were the work of individuals at academic institutions including UNLV, the University of Nevada-Reno, Ohio State University and the University of St Andrews.

claims.source: https://ufos-scientificresearch.blogspot.com/2022/03/37-out-of-those-38-aawsap-defense.html (Keith Basterfield, 23 March 2022, quoting the DIA response)
claims.text: A 2022 DIA FOIA response produced 37 of the 38 DIRDs; the one withheld is a classified version of another document in the set. DIA told the requester: 'we plan to release all AATIP related documents to the DIA FOIA Reading Room. I don't have the exact number of documents, however I do know it will be more than 37.'

Three DIRDs circulated publicly before the FOIA release: 'Advanced Space Propulsion' and 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions' posted in late 2017, and 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, And Negative Energy' separately.

claims.source: LinkedIn posting archived and quoted at https://hm05uap.substack.com/p/2025-uap-records-in-review (31 December 2025); original at https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/counterintelligence-and-humint-operations-officer-senior-at-booz-allen-hamilton-4316384294/
claims.text: In 2025 Booz Allen Hamilton posted a TS/SCI 'Counterintelligence and HUMINT Operations Officer, Senior' role requiring experience conducting comprehensive records reviews of U.S. government agencies 'including archived and classified materials, for information about Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) activities,' the ability to execute 'site surveys of government facilities, archives, and locations linked to alleged historical UAP activity,' and the ability to prepare input for 'congressionally mandated reports such as the Historical Record Report.' The posting was live for under a week.

connections: Robert Bigelow -> BAASS -> Bigelow Aerospace -> National Institute for Discovery Science (NIDSci) -> Skinwalker Ranch, the same corporate lineage that later held the AAWSAP field-investigation work.

Hal Puthoff and Eric Davis -> EarthTech International -> To The Stars Academy alongside Luis Elizondo, connecting the research contractor, the DIA program office and the 2017 public disclosure vehicle through shared personnel.
James T. Lacatski (DIA) is the government official who converted the BAASS deliverables into DIRDs, tying the collection to a single named custodian.
Senators John McCain and Jack Reed (SASC) generated the list; Steven Aftergood (FAS) forced its release; Nick Pope and George Knapp published parallel copies.

Kit Green (former CIA) and George Hathaway appear in the author network, linking the DIRDs to the anomalous-materials analysis lineage that surfaces again in Garry Nolan's seat on the 2026 UAP Science Advisory Council.
Marc Millis (ex-NASA, Tau Zero Foundation) links the DIRD collection directly to NASA's institutional periphery.
Lockheed Martin and Directed Technologies, Inc. are the named prime-contractor participants; the only classified DIRD came from the Directed Technologies laser work.
George Knapp, who published the first near-complete DIRD list in July 2018, testified before Rep. Luna's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets on 9 September 2025.
Booz Allen Hamilton's 2025 UAP records-review role indicates the contractor-executed historical records function continued into the AARO Historical Record Report era.
dossier.denialPosture: DIA has not denied the existence of the series; it released thirty-seven of thirty-eight papers under FOIA in March 2022. Its release documentation made no reference to the classified SECRET version of the high-energy laser weapons report, neither producing it nor logging it as withheld. AARO's position is that the papers are unreviewed exploratory surveys tasked under the contract's stated aerospace-threat scope.
dossier.narrative:
There is a way of reading the DIRD series that makes it the single most informative document set on this board, and it is simply to read the titles in order and ask what question they collectively answer.

The released thirty-seven include 'Metallic Glasses - Status and Prospects for Aerospace Applications,' 'Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter,' 'Materials for Advanced Aerospace Platforms,' 'Metamaterials for Aerospace Applications' and 'Metallic Spintronics' - the materials question. They include 'Positron Aerospace Propulsion,' 'Inertial Electrostatic Confinement Fusion,' 'Advanced Nuclear Propulsion For Manned Deep Space Missions,' 'Negative Mass Propulsion,' 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion,' 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II,' 'MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications' and 'Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites' - the propulsion question. They include 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions,' 'Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering,' 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy,' 'The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research,' 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications,' 'Concepts for Extracting Energy From the Quantum Vacuum' and 'Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum' - the physics-you-would-need question. They include 'Invisibility Cloaking - Theory and Experiments' and 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities' - signature and detection. And they include 'Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues,' 'Biosensors and BioMEMS,' 'Biomaterials,' 'Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices,' 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft' and 'Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight' - the human question, which is to say, what happens to a person near one of these, and what would it be like to be inside one.

That is not a random reading list. It maps one to one onto the twelve technical areas in the AAWSAP statement of objectives: lift, propulsion, control, power generation, spatial and temporal translation, materials, configuration and structure, signature reduction, human interface, human effects, armament, and peripheral areas. The DIRDs are the deliverable structure of the contract made visible. And two of the titles are difficult to explain by any framing other than the one this board starts from. 'Anomalous Acute and Subacute Field Effects on Human Biological Tissues' is a medical paper about injury from proximity to something. 'Cockpits in the Era of Breakthrough Flight' is a human factors paper about operating a vehicle that does not exist.

The release history is its own artefact. Eric Davis, who worked for Bigelow Aerospace and BAASS, said on Coast to Coast AM on 28 January 2018 that thirty-eight such reports had been produced under AAWSAP. Within forty-eight hours The Black Vault filed for all of them; the request became FOIA case FOIA-0159-2018. In January 2019 a listing breakdown of the reports arrived under a separate case, FOIA-0033-2019, though a slightly different version of the list had already leaked. DIA completed the main request more than four years later, on 25 March 2022, releasing thirty-seven of the thirty-eight. The one that did not come out was the SECRET-classified version of 'State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons.' Critically, it was not listed as withheld. The release letter did not reference it at all, which is why the appeal was filed on the adequacy of DIA's search rather than on the applicability of an exemption - a procedurally different and, for a board about concealment, a more interesting posture. An unclassified version of that same paper, DIRD 23, is in the released set at thirty-one pages.

The DIRDs also function as a personnel map. The authorship of the series connects the private technical layer catalogued elsewhere on this board directly to a DIA contract: the space-time metric engineering and quantum vacuum papers, the wormhole and warp drive papers, and the materials papers were written by named specialists who reappear later at To The Stars Academy, at EarthTech International, and in the disclosure hearings of 2023 to 2025. The government did not go to a federal laboratory or an FFRDC for this survey. It went to a small network of physicists with an existing interest in the subject, through a small business set-aside contract, performed at the contractor's own facility.

What the series does not contain is equally important and should be stated plainly. No DIRD reports an examination of recovered material. No DIRD describes a craft. They are literature surveys and theoretical assessments, and several of them conclude that the routes they examine are not presently achievable. AARO's characterisation is that they were 'exploratory papers addressing the 12 scientific areas tasked in the contract's statement of work' which 'were never thoroughly peer reviewed.' On the face of the documents, that is accurate.

The argument for their place on this map is therefore not that they contain the secret. It is that they define its shape. A government office that believed it was looking at nothing would not commission a paper on the acute and subacute effects of anomalous fields on human biological tissue. A programme whose only interest was foreign aerospace threat out to 2050 would not need a survey of traversable wormholes. The DIRDs are the negative space around an object: thirty-eight independent attempts to explain, from first principles, how something that had already been observed could possibly work.
openQuestions: The status of the thirty-eighth document, the SECRET version of 'State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons,' and the outcome of the adequacy-of-search appeal.
The internal DIA tasking record: who chose the thirty-eight topics, when, and against what requirement. No topic-selection memorandum has been released.
Whether the DIRDs were circulated, cited or acted upon anywhere in DoD or the Intelligence Community after publication, or whether they were shelved on delivery.
Whether any of the DIRD authors held or were offered special-access read-ins in connection with the work, which would connect the unclassified series to a classified effort.

Whether the 'proposals to set up laboratories to examine any recovered UFO materials' that AARO says the contractor made are documented anywhere alongside the DIRD tasking, and whether any DIRD topic was selected in support of such a laboratory.
What is the 38th document, and is the withheld classified version the only classified product of the contract or the only one acknowledged?
Did BAASS produce deliverables outside the 38 — in particular the field-investigation and case-database work described by participants — and under what contract line?
What was the total AAWSAP contract value and ceiling, and what was the sole-source justification for awarding it to BAASS?
Who at DIA selected the topic list, and was there a technical merit review that overrode the 2008 JASON assessment of HFGW?
Were classified companion analyses produced under a different program element, and if so which one?
Who was the client for the 2025 Booz Allen UAP records-review and site-survey role, and was it AARO, the PURSUE Task Force, or a congressional deliverable?
Which 'locations linked to alleged historical UAP activity' were to be site-surveyed under that contract?
dossier.whatItIs: The Defense Intelligence Reference Documents are a series of approximately thirty-eight unclassified technical survey papers commissioned from outside specialists under the AAWSAP contract and published by the Defense Intelligence Agency between roughly 2009 and 2011. They cover metamaterials, warp drive, traversable wormholes, antigravity, negative mass propulsion, quantum vacuum energy extraction, invisibility cloaking, high-frequency gravitational wave communications, and human biological effects of anomalous fields. Thirty-seven of the thirty-eight were released to The Black Vault by DIA on 25 March 2022 under FOIA case FOIA-0159-2018.
dossier.whyImplicated: The DIRDs are the most literal artefact on this board: a list, written by the United States government's own defence intelligence agency, of every theoretical route by which the observed flight performance of anomalous objects might be achieved. Read as a set, they are not a scattershot survey but a systematic decomposition of a capability - lift without visible propulsion, translation in space and time, signature reduction, materials that do not behave conventionally, and the effects such a craft would have on a human body standing near it. The government commissioned this taxonomy in 2008 and 2009 while the same contract was running field investigation teams and proposing laboratories to examine recovered material. One of the thirty-eight, the classified SECRET version of 'State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons,' has never been released and was not even acknowledged as withheld in the release letter, which is why the requester appealed on the adequacy of the search rather than on an exemption.

entityInfo.desc: Release-number cross-walk. The DIA transmittal order (used in the 9 January 2018 letter to the Senate Armed Services Committee) does NOT match the numbering of the publicly released PDFs, which follow the order in which DIA processed them for FOIA. Selected mappings between released DIRD number and transmittal item: released DIRD 15 = transmittal item 5 (Puthoff, spacetime metric engineering); released DIRD 18 = item 8 (Davis, traversable wormholes); released DIRD 19 = item 11 (Davis, antigravity); released DIRD 24 = item 14 (Davis, quantum vacuum energy); released DIRD 26 = item 12 (Green, field effects on biological tissues); released DIRD 27 = item 31 (Davis, laser lightcraft nanosatellites); released DIRD 36 = item 34 (Davis, quantum tomography of negative energy states); released DIRD 13 = item 19 (Obousy, warp drive); released DIRD 21 = item 9 (Baker, high-frequency gravitational wave communications); released DIRD 23 = items 37/38 (Albertine, high-energy laser weapons — only the unclassified version released). Researchers citing these documents should give both the transmittal item number and the released DIRD file number, because the two numbering systems are routinely conflated in secondary sources.
